http_response.description: 60-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and adalimumab, admitted after a burn from an electric heater. Four months earlier she developed pain and stiffness in the MCP and interphalangeal joints, right ankle, and both knees. Six weeks before admission she had severe arthralgia, low-grade fever, livedo reticularis on the legs, and purpuric lesions around the malleoli. Labs then showed anemia, leukopenia/neutropenia, elevated rheumatoid factor, hypergammaglobulinemia, positive ANA, low C4, mildly positive anti-dsDNA, and positive cryoglobulins; HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests were negative. On admission she had fever and pancytopenia, without hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy; blood film, cultures, chest/abdomen/pelvis CT, CMV PCR, and tuberculin test were negative. She had traveled to Athens 7 months earlier and stayed with relatives who kept several dogs.
